question: With real multi-LUN traffic and 1 TB platters: how large should the read-ahead buffer (K) be, and how much does an LRU platter cache next to the reader (C) save?
trace: Fujitsu SYSTOR'17 VDI traces (Lee et al.), 2016-02-22 07-20 JST, LUNs 0,1,2,3,4,6, reads only; first 5 s of each hourly file dropped (README: packet loss at hour changes)
library: 640 slots (8 rows x 80), 1 reader, 8 Zone shuttles, B1 Silica scheduler; every platter holds 1 TB; slots without traced data hold other rarely read data

placements.contig_1tb: primary: each LUN written sequentially, 1 TB per platter, platters at random rack positions
placements.random_1gib: sensitivity / worst case: every 1 GiB extent on a random platter

sampling.note: 2000 reads drawn uniformly from 10 trace minutes, order kept; the trace serves ~2,700 reads/s, a glass library ~1/s, so the stream must be thinned

load_note: time axis stretched so the mean arrival rate = load x B1 throughput (K=8, C=0, all arrivals at t=0) of the same placement
